newsitem.title: QATAR: U.S. trade with GCC up 14 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: U.S. trade with GCC up 14 percent in 1996.

text.p: A U.S. official said on Sunday that trade between his country and the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states grew by about 14 percent in 1996 compared to a year earlier.
"The volume of trade between the two regions has now topped $25 billion annually -- about 14 percent higher than 1995," Jan Kalicki, counselor at the U.S. Commerce Department, said.

"U.S. exports to the Gulf countries grew by an estimated 22 percent last year, reaching $12.34 billion, while the U.S. investment (in the region) totalled $4 billion in 1995, an increase of 26 percent over the preceding year," Kalicki told a news conference in Doha.
Kalicki is heading a U.S. trade delegation touring the region since February 28.
The tour which started in Oman, will also take him to Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Yemen.
"I think much can still be done, not only in the area of trade but in the area of investments", Kalicki said.
He said Gulf states should implement product standards consistent with those of the U.S. and eliminate other obstacles such as agency-distributor requirements.
The GCC, an economic and political alliance, includes Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, UAE and Qatar.
